**Test Credentials**
| Merchant Till | Secret Key | Status |
|----------------|------------|--------|
| 133238 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
| 133239 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
| 133240 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |
**Integration steps**

**Step 1 — Get authorization.**

 Obtain an OAuth2 bearer token with your
API credentials and send it as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`
on every call. Obtain a fresh token before it expires — an expired
token is rejected before the signature is even checked.

**Step 2 — Sign the payload.**

Build the canonical string
`merchantTill|timestamp|nonce` (pipe-joined, no whitespace) and
compute the lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 digest of it, keyed with the
till's secret. `limit` is NOT part of the canonical string. Generate
`timestamp` and `nonce` fresh for every call, including repeat
pulls of the same till. The scheme is identical across the LOOP
Matrix APIs — an implementation built for Send Money or Transaction
Inquiry works here unchanged.

```python
import hmac, hashlib, uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Issued to your till at onboarding — never transmitted in the request
SECRET_KEY = "<your_secret_key>"
MERCHANT_TILL = "<your_merchantTill>"

# Generate fresh values for every call, including repeat pulls
timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
nonce = str(uuid.uuid4()).lower()

# Canonical string: merchantTill|timestamp|nonce (limit is excluded)
message = f"{MERCHANT_TILL}|{timestamp}|{nonce}"

signature = hmac.new(
    SECRET_KEY.encode("utf-8"),
    message.encode("utf-8"),
    hashlib.sha256
).hexdigest()  # lowercase hex — not Base64

# timestamp, nonce and signature go inside requestParameters
```

Verify your implementation against this worked example before
sending a live request — same inputs must reproduce the same
signature: secret key `hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8`,
merchantTill `133239`, timestamp `2026-07-21T08:47:12Z`, nonce
`c2a91b7e-4d05-4f8a-a3c6-9e1f5d7b2a48` -> signature
`8b48798149f4f71095dabbeea88c116730fb56f18c90970b39d992442f9561c9`.

**Step 3 — Build the request body.**

Assemble the service envelope
(`serviceCode`, `txnReference`, `requestParameters`) with the signed
`timestamp`, `nonce` and `signature` nested inside
`requestParameters` alongside `merchantTill` and `limit`. The
envelope `txnReference` identifies this history call itself, not a
transaction — every call needs a fresh one, and the transactions in
the response each carry their own references that are never sent in
the request. See TransactionHistoryRequest below.

**Step 4 — Send the request.**

POST the signed body with your bearer
token to `/services/process-request`. There is no `callBackUrl` on
this endpoint — the call is fully synchronous, and the transaction
list comes back in this response.

**Step 5 — Read the response.**

Branch on the `statusCode` field
inside the response body, not the HTTP status line — the gateway
returns HTTP 200 for almost every outcome, handled failures
included. `count` tells you how many transactions actually came
back, which can be lower than `limit`. See the statusCode table on
the 200 response below.

**Step 6 — Process each item, and pair with Transaction Inquiry.**

 Transactions are returned most recent first, each with its own
`status` and `finalState`. Process each on its own merits; for any
item whose `finalState` is false, follow it up individually with
the Transaction Inquiry API (MRCHNT_TXN_INQUIRY) rather than
assuming it has settled. A common pattern: sweep the history on a
schedule, then poll Inquiry on any still-in-flight item's
reference until it settles.

**Step 7 — Handle failures and retries.**

 Because the retrieval is
read-only, retrying is always safe. On a statusCode 404 (duplicate
envelope reference) or 504 (gateway timeout), retry with a fresh
envelope `txnReference` and fresh security parameters — the
opposite of the payment products, where a retry reuses the original
reference. On a statusCode 401, check the till and re-sign before
retrying.

**Step 8 — Test in sandbox, then go live.**

 Sandbox accepts only
merchant tills 133238, 133239 and 133240, sharing one sandbox
secret key; any other till is rejected with statusCode 401.
Production tills, secrets and endpoint URL are issued per merchant
at onboarding — everything else about the contract stays the same.

response.name:
The gateway returns HTTP 200 for essentially every outcome, success or handled failure — the authoritative result is the `statusCode` field in the response body, not the HTTP status line:

| statusCode | Meaning | Returned when |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Success | The retrieval was executed and the transaction list is in data. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | The till is not registered to you, or the signature, timestamp or nonce did not verify. |
| 404 | Duplicate reference | The envelope txnReference of this history call has been used before. |

data is an empty object `{}` on every non-200 statusCode.

response.name: Gateway timeout. The upstream service did not respond in time. Carries a request_id instead of a data object. Because the retrieval is read-only, retrying is always safe — use a fresh envelope txnReference and fresh security parameters.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Merchant Transaction History — retrieve the most recent transactions on
a merchant till (payments, payouts and other activity), each with its
status, amount, timestamps and references, via Mapping Service. Fully
synchronous and read-only: no money moves, there is no callback, and
the list comes back in the response to this single call. Companion API
to Transaction Inquiry (MRCHNT_TXN_INQUIRY) — use History to see recent
activity on a till, and Inquiry to follow one specific transaction to
its terminal state.
See the Integration steps in the operation description below.
